turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Why do you refuse to play, boy?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Because I am not accustomed to playing with ladies, and I fear I may make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Nonsense, child, you will play with Estella, and you will make no mistakes.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, ma'am, I am not sure I am worthy of playing with Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Worthy? You are worthy, indeed. You are a common boy, and you will play with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am but a poor boy, ma'am, and I do not wish to trouble Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will trouble her not at all, boy. You will play, and you will be merry.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Now, call Estella, that we may begin.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Estella is at the door, ma'am, waiting to be summoned.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Then, call her in, that we may play.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, ma'am, I do not wish to intrude upon Miss Estella's leisure.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will not intrude, boy. You will play with Estella, and I will watch.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I do not wish to play, ma'am, if it is not agreeable to Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will play with you, and she will be delighted.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Call her in, boy, that we may begin.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Very well, ma'am, I will call her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ah, yes, now Estella will join us, and we will play.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will watch, and I will see how you play.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am not sure I am worthy of Miss Estella's attention, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Worthy? You are worthy, indeed. You will play with Estella, and you will be merry.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy and had come to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer and let her look at him.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not afraid.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched when she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he knew it was her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that her heart was broken.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired and wanted diversion.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies and had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham repeatedly told Pip to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not sullen and obstinate, but was very sorry for Miss Havisham and could not play just now.
